note: The candidate MLE Network Data TLV length controls how many network-data bytes are copied from the received message into the leader network-data buffer.
A stored Network Data TLV is interpreted as a Prefix TLV and its candidate-controlled prefix length is later used for prefix matching.
The prefix TLV validity relation permits a prefix length whose byte count fits the TLV but does not require the bit length to be at most the 128-bit IPv6 address size.
The unchecked prefix length is passed as the maximum number of bits that PrefixMatch should compare against a 16-byte IPv6 address.
When the prefix length requires more than 16 bytes, the loop reads past the end of the 16-byte IPv6 address array b.
